jtechstorage.guide.welcome.title: Welcome!
jtechstorage.guide.welcome.body:
Glad you're here! JTechStorage connects your ordinary chests into a network – no power, no cables. On top of that: amethyst helpers, teams and trade, phoenix mail, two bosses and gear from the End.

This handbook explains the controls. Recipes, creatures, items and bosses have their own books – see "Library".

Mod by %s
jtechstorage.guide.start.title: Getting Started
jtechstorage.guide.start.body:
1. Place a Storage Terminal.
2. Shift + right-click it with a Storage Key to link.
3. Shift + right-click chests to add them.
4. Open the terminal – done!

jtechstorage.tutorial.step.0: Hey! I'm Jbartels – I built JTechStorage. Let me quickly show you what the mod can do. (Right-click me = next, Shift + right-click = skip)
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.1: The heart of the mod is the Storage Terminal. It connects your normal vanilla chests into one network – see and take everything in one place, no power needed.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.2: With the Storage Key you bind yourself to the terminal (Shift + right-click) and add chests (Shift + right-click on the chest). While you hold it, all linked chests sparkle.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.3: The Crafting Terminal refills its grid from storage after every craft. An item frame turns a chest into a sorting chest. With the Team and Trade Terminals you share your storage with friends or open a shop.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.4: The first upgrades can't be crafted – you have to earn them! Use the Resonance Igniter and defeat the Amethyst Robot. With some luck it drops an Amethyst Core – you need one for every helper.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.5: The Wireless Terminal opens your network from afar – but only with a Wireless Core. With some luck the Amethyst Robot drops that too.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.6: The Amethyst Sprite sorts your chests by category, collects dropped items, tidies chests inside and empties placed backpacks.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.7: The Watch Moth keeps watch at night: it makes monsters glow, warns you with a bell and shows Peter his targets.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.8: The Storage Griffin is your flying mount with a chest. Land within terminal range and it unloads everything.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.9: The Spark Beetle charges your terminal with resonance. Resonance is only a bonus: more range, faster helpers – and no night break.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.10: This is Chel – named after my best friend. He crafts missing items automatically. Give him a diamond for a joke … and try a nether star.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.11: Peter Chel Parker – Chel's hero form. He protects your base from monsters. With a Dragon Heart, Peter even becomes Cheldrogan, a dragon you can ride and fly.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.12: And this is Ashley. She's … well, a bit dirty. When Peter is hurt, he kicks her to heal. She (mostly) doesn't hold it against him.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.13: The Phoenix is your mail carrier: it lives in a Phoenix Nest and carries parcels from your storage straight into your friends' storage.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.14: With an Amethyst Obsidian Upgrade it becomes the Amethyst Phoenix: two seats, up to four chests. Build up to four Phoenix Stops, name them and set the order with a Flight Plan – it then flies the route on its own.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.15: Crystal Lairs float in the outer End – the Lair Compass shows the way. The Great Amethyst Spider guards them. Every victory grants an upgrade for Amethyst Obsidian gear: better than netherite, with a set bonus.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.16: Every few days the Amethyst Fox digs up an enchanted book – with crystal enchantments like Double Jump or Recall that exist nowhere else.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.17: Backpacks come in five sizes. Upgrading keeps the contents, and you can dye them, wear them on your back or place them as a block – and they pick up matching items automatically.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.18: You can recolor your helpers with dye and give them hats. And the gear button in the terminal sets the theme, accent color and size of all mod screens.
jtechstorage.tutorial.step.19: That's it! All recipes and details are in the Storage Handbook. Shift + right-click with the handbook brings me back. Have fun!

Crystal Lairs float in the outer End. The Lair Compass (right-click in the End) points to the nearest one.

On your first visit the Great Amethyst Spider awakens (600 health): venom bite, leap, crystal webs, ground spikes, shriek. Below 50 %% she calls spiderlings.

jtechstorage.guide.fox.title: Amethyst Fox
jtechstorage.guide.fox.body:
Place the fox and link it with a bound key. About every three days it digs in dirt, sand or gravel during the day and finds an enchanted book with a crystal enchantment – available nowhere else. The book goes into your storage.

Feeding speeds it up: glow berries −6 h, sweet berries −3 h (up to 4× per day). Sneak + right-click with an empty hand = pack up.
jtechstorage.guide.crystal_enchants.body:
Double Jump (boots, I–II): jump again in mid-air.
Sprint (leggings, I–III): faster while sprinting.
Recall (storage key): right-click into the air to return to the terminal once per day.
Careful Touch (pickaxe): mines monster spawners with their mob and budding amethyst.
Life Spark (sword/axe, I–III): melee hits heal you a little.

Only from the Amethyst Fox, apply with an anvil.

jtechstorage.guide.terminal.title: Using the Terminal
jtechstorage.guide.terminal.body:
Left click: stack · Right click: half · Shift-click: to inventory. Click with an item in hand: store it.

Search: name, enchantment (e.g. "sharpness v"), $enchantment, @mod, #tag. Right-click the search box to clear it.

Tabs on the left: filter by category (click the active tab again or right-click = all).

Crafting Terminal: the grid refills from storage, "×" empties it. Wireless Terminal (with Wireless Core): Shift + right-click the terminal to bind, then right-click in the air.

Statistics button (right of the hotbar): fill level, history, categories and today's changes.

jtechstorage.guide.interface.body:
The gear button in the terminal (below the upgrade slots) opens the settings for all mod screens:

jtechstorage.guide.cheldrogan.title: Cheldrogan
jtechstorage.guide.cheldrogan.body:
Dragon Heart on Peter Chel Parker: he becomes Cheldrogan, a hovering crystal serpent dragon with crystal antlers and a resonance pearl.

Right-click = mount. Space = take off, in the air he flies where you look.

Left click = tail sweep: he spins once around himself and hurls everything nearby away.
R = crystal breath: a beam that follows your gaze. Where it hits, resonance crystals grow from the ground and encase monsters for a few seconds.
V = crystal shard rain: he rears up and amethyst shards rain down on the spot you aim at.

Without a rider he guards the base like Peter and heals at Ashley. At night he coils up. Dismount far away and that becomes his new base. At 0 health he turns back into Peter.

jtechstorage.guide.phoenix_stops.title: Stops & Flight Plan
jtechstorage.guide.phoenix_stops.body:
1. Build Phoenix Stops (up to 4) and right-click to name them. That is also where you set the rest time: 30 seconds, 5 minutes or one night.
2. Click the stops with a Flight Plan in the order you want.
3. Right-click in the air: reorder or remove stops.
4. Right-click the Amethyst Phoenix with the Flight Plan.

It lands on top of the blocks, visits the stops in order and then starts over.

Delivery order: put chests or barrels right next to the stop and pick Unload, Load or Both in its window. Up to 9 filters decide which items – and, with the scroll wheel, how many per visit.

jtechstorage.guide.chronicle.title: Crystal Chronicle
jtechstorage.guide.chronicle.body:
Deep within amethyst sleeps an ancient resonance. Whoever wakes it meets guardians of crystal – and treasures stronger than netherite.

This chronicle tells the legend and covers the bosses, Amethyst Obsidian, the crystal enchantments and the evolutions of the helpers.
jtechstorage.guide.legend.title: The Resonance
jtechstorage.guide.legend.body:
Amethyst sings. Listen closely and you'll notice it in every shard – a quiet hum that connects things.

The helpers were born from this resonance: small creatures with a core of pure amethyst. But the resonance also created guardians. The Amethyst Robot sleeps until a Resonance Igniter wakes it. And in the outer End, in floating crystal lairs, the Great Amethyst Spider lurks above the most precious material of all: Amethyst Obsidian.
jtechstorage.guide.evolutions.title: Evolutions
jtechstorage.guide.evolutions.body:
Chel → Peter Chel Parker: right-click Chel with a nether star.

Peter → Cheldrogan: right-click Peter with a Dragon Heart. At 0 health Cheldrogan turns back into Peter, and Peter into Chel.

Phoenix → Amethyst Phoenix: right-click a phoenix with an Amethyst Obsidian Upgrade.

Owner and network are kept with every evolution.
jtechstorage.guide.roadmap.title: Roadmap
jtechstorage.guide.roadmap.body:
1. Terminal, key, first chests.
2. Build a Resonance Igniter, defeat the Amethyst Robot: iron upgrades, Amethyst and Wireless Cores.
3. First helpers: sprite, moth, griffin, beetle, Chel, Ashley.
4. Team and Trade Terminals, phoenix mail.
5. Evolve Chel into Peter with a nether star.
6. Find a crystal lair in the End and defeat the Great Amethyst Spider.
7. Amethyst Obsidian gear, Amethyst Phoenix, Amethyst Fox.
8. Dragon Heart: Cheldrogan.

jtechstorage.lexicon.storage_terminal: The heart of your network. It lists the items of all linked chests with search, category tabs and sorting. Upgrades go into the terminal's slots and raise range and chest count.
jtechstorage.lexicon.crafting_terminal: A Storage Terminal with a 3×3 grid. Ingredients are refilled from storage, "×" puts everything back. With JEI, "+" transfers whole recipes.
jtechstorage.lexicon.team_terminal: Manages the team of a network: name, color, access, members with roles (Guest to Owner) and channel messages in chat.
jtechstorage.lexicon.trade_terminal: A shop with six "goods for price" offers. Goods come from your storage, payment goes into it – even while you're offline.
jtechstorage.lexicon.phoenix_nest: The mail address of a storage. The phoenix lives here: pick a destination, place items, send. Parcels for you land in storage.
jtechstorage.lexicon.phoenix_stop: A landing spot for the Amethyst Phoenix. Every stop needs a name and has its own rest time: 30 seconds, 5 minutes or one night. With a delivery order, the phoenix exchanges items with the chests right next to it when it lands – unload, load or both, optionally filtered and with an amount per visit.
jtechstorage.lexicon.crystal_altar: Stands in the heart of every crystal lair in the End. A Crystal Cocoon on it summons the Great Amethyst Spider again.
jtechstorage.lexicon.storage_key: Your most important tool: it binds to a terminal, adds chests and links helpers and extra terminals to the network.
jtechstorage.lexicon.wireless_terminal: Opens your storage from afar. Only works with a Wireless Core installed. With an Ender upgrade in the terminal it reaches everywhere – even other dimensions.
jtechstorage.lexicon.flight_plan: Sets the route of the Amethyst Phoenix: up to four named stops in any order. In its window (right-click in the air) you reorder or remove stops.
jtechstorage.lexicon.leather_backpack: Backpacks come in five tiers from 9 to 54 slots. Wear them in the chest slot, dye them and place them as a block. Items that are already inside get picked up automatically.
jtechstorage.lexicon.amethyst_draught: The Resonance Igniter wakes the Amethyst Robot. Only use it once you're well equipped!
jtechstorage.lexicon.lair_compass: Points to the nearest crystal lair in the End, home of the Great Amethyst Spider.
jtechstorage.lexicon.crystal_cocoon: Placed on the Crystal Altar, it summons the Great Amethyst Spider again – for another Amethyst Obsidian Upgrade.
jtechstorage.lexicon.amethyst_core: The core of every helper. Not craftable – only dropped by the Amethyst Robot.

jtechstorage.guide.storm.title: The Resonance Storm
jtechstorage.guide.storm.body:
A Resonance Storm moves over a Storage Terminal. It starts on its own when you stand in the chunk of your own terminal, have at least one helper and have mined more than 500 amethyst since your last storm (at most once per in-game day). Thunder, purple-red sparks and a boss bar announce it.

While it rages, your network is disturbed: half range, helpers work at half speed and resonance charge is drained.

Crystal Shardlings attack in three waves; in the last wave the Storm Herald appears. Defeat it and the storm ends at once.

Peter Chel Parker, Cheldrogan and the Watch Moths defend the base with you.

Shatters into shards when it dies. When the storm ends, all remaining shardlings crumble.

Leader of the Resonance Storm. It hovers just above the ground, keeps its distance and hurls resonance bolts. When shardlings run low, it summons new ones.

Its death ends the storm. Loot: amethyst, amethyst blocks and, with some luck, an Amethyst Core.

jtechstorage.guide.storm_legend.title: The Storm
jtechstorage.guide.storm_legend.body:
Not every resonance is a song. Sometimes it rings false – then the amethyst splinters, and from the splinters crawl creatures that want only one thing: to silence the heart of a storage.

The old ones called it the Resonance Storm. Its herald carries a cracked tuning fork. As long as it rings, the network stays out of tune.

That is why every base needs a protector.

jtechstorage.guide.crystal_wolf.title: Crystal Wolf
jtechstorage.guide.crystal_wolf.body:
Feed your tamed wolf an Amethyst Core – it becomes a Crystal Wolf.

Once linked it guards the base (20 blocks around the terminal): it attacks monsters, herds stray farm animals back and brings monster loot (bones, string, gunpowder …) into storage.

Crystal Wolves fight harder in a pack. At night they sleep in a Wolf Basket – if monsters come close or a Resonance Storm rages, they wake at once.

Bone: follow or guard the base. Meat: heal. If its health drops too low it retreats exhausted – it cannot die.
jtechstorage.guide.moon_wolf.title: Moon Wolf
jtechstorage.guide.moon_wolf.body:
Once you have a pack of at least 5 Crystal Wolves of your own, a Moon Wolf sometimes appears on a hill near your base on full-moon nights. At dawn it disappears again.

Win it over with an Amethyst Bone. It leads the pack: Crystal Wolves near it bite harder.

Right-click with a compass: it scents the nearest structure (village, mineshaft, ruined portal, treasure, trial chambers, ancient city).

During a Resonance Storm it lets out its moon howl: storm creatures freeze for a moment and the pack grows stronger and faster.
jtechstorage.guide.helper_home.title: Helper Home
jtechstorage.guide.helper_home.body:
Place Helper Beds and Wolf Baskets near the terminal (16 blocks).

At night every helper picks its own free sleeping spot of its kind, reserves it and sleeps in it: the small helpers in a Helper Bed, the wolves in a Wolf Basket. If none is free, it lies down on the ground.

The griffin, the phoenixes and Cheldrogan do not need a bed.

jtechstorage.guide.companions.title: Companions
jtechstorage.guide.companions.body:
Deep inside amethyst geodes there sometimes lives a Geode Keeper. He gives you one of three companions: Mantis (strongest fighter), Shroom (heals) or Raven (carries). He also trades like a villager (shift + right-click, or a plain right-click once you have a companion): amethyst shards for treats, Amethyst Cores, budding amethyst and more – the more you trade, the better the offers he unlocks. Once you accept a companion or trade with him, he stays in his geode for good. All three fight at your side – the raven with 70 %, the shroom with a quarter of the mantis' strength. If you don't like his offer, decline and look for another geode. You can only have one companion.

Right-click: follow/stay, the G key works from a distance too. At stage 3 you can ride the mantis and the raven (right-click). The K key or Shift + right-click opens the companion menu (raven: Shift + right-click opens the bag). It follows you everywhere, even through portals and after death.

Half of the experience you collect goes to it. At level 30 it reaches stage 2, at level 100 stage 3. It doesn't die – when it takes too much damage it is exhausted for a moment.

/jtechstorage companion call (or "Call" in the menu) brings it to you – even from another dimension or from unloaded areas. It only comes where there is solid ground; while you fly it waits until you have landed.

The companion menu shows level, health and stats, lets you choose a stance (aggressive, defensive or passive) and spend talent points: one every 4 levels, up to 30. Each species has three branches with five talents each (deeper ones need the talent above and sometimes stage 2 or 3) and a Special branch, where you pick exactly one of three special attacks that you trigger in combat with the B key. Resetting costs an Amethyst Core. The Look tab customizes it (see "Look and equipment"), and your bond grows by feeding, petting and playing (see "Bond"). A small HUD in the top left shows your companion's state (can be turned off in the menu).
jtechstorage.guide.geode_keeper.title: Geode Keeper
jtechstorage.guide.geode_keeper.body:
An old hermit with crystals on his shoulders and a staff topped with a cracked geode. Every geode has exactly one chance that he lives there – you hear a soft hum when you are close.

Right-click: he offers you a companion. Accept or decline by clicking in chat. If you decline he disappears; otherwise he never leaves on his own. He can be killed (he drops nothing) and moved in a boat or minecart. Shift + right-click (or a plain right-click once you have a companion) opens his trades – he trades like a villager and unlocks better offers the more you trade.
jtechstorage.guide.mantis.title: Shadow Mantis
jtechstorage.guide.mantis.body:
A pitch-black praying mantis with glowing eyes, serrated claws and swept-back horns. Fights at your side against everything you attack or that attacks you, and against monsters near you (it leaves creepers alone).

Stage 1: youngling. Stage 2: grown up with dorsal spikes, a cobra hood and leather wings, more damage and knockback. Stage 3 (Blade Queen): spiked pauldrons, a crown, amethyst scythes and crystal wings; its scythe strike also hits monsters around the target.

At stage 3 you can ride it: hold Space to fly briefly (about 4 s), then it glides down and recharges on the ground.

In your base (3×3 chunks around your own terminal) it fights 50% harder. Tell it to stay there and it stands guard: it patrols around the terminal and attacks monsters within 24 blocks – even while you are away.
jtechstorage.guide.shroom.title: Amethyst Shroom
jtechstorage.guide.shroom.body:
A mushroom on two legs with glowing spots on its cap. Heals you when you are hurt – automatically or only on key press: H heals right away, Shift + H switches between automatic and key. Afterwards it needs a break (stage 1: 30 s, 2: 20 s, 3: 15 s).

Stage 1: sits on your shoulder and does not fight yet, gives regeneration. Stage 2: 2 hearts instantly + regeneration, also for your pets and companions. Stage 3 (with a backpack and a healing potion): 3 hearts + regeneration II, removes poison and wither, heals all players nearby and saves you at low health (automatic mode only).

From stage 2 it fights only from a distance: it keeps away and hurls spore bolts (up to 10 blocks, 12 at stage 3) – with a quarter of the mantis' strength.

In your base (3×3 chunks around your own terminal) it makes crops grow faster from stage 2, and at stage 3 you can fly there like in creative mode.
jtechstorage.guide.raven.title: Night Raven
jtechstorage.guide.raven.body:
A jet-black raven with glowing eyes, a spiky ruff and a courier bag. At stage 3 (Raven Lord) it wears a bone mask, horns, a crystal crest and a saddle. Collects items around you (stage 1: 9 slots, 2: 18, 3: 27; larger radius per stage) and pecks at monsters with quick strikes (70 % of the mantis' strength).

Right-click with a bound Storage Key links it to the terminal. When its bag is two-thirds full it flies the items there – clicking with the key again sends it right away. Shift + right-click opens the bag. At stage 1 it sits on your left shoulder, flies off to fight and comes back afterwards.

In the companion menu you can send it exploring (4 minutes, then a 5-minute rest): it brings back finds – stage 1 copper and iron, stage 2 gold, emeralds and redstone, stage 3 diamonds, ender pearls and rarities.

At stage 3 it is big enough to carry you: right-click to mount, it flies where you look for as long as you like.

Passive abilities (always active, stronger with every level): Crow Scatter – when hit, it sometimes bursts into crows, takes no damage and reassembles a few blocks away (10–35 %). Scout Crows – small shadow crows circle you, make nearby monsters glow and warn you of creepers behind you. Guardian Crow – sometimes intercepts arrows and other projectiles that would hit you (15–35 %). Crow Double – a hit that would kill you makes you burst into crows instead: a shadow decoy stays for 6 seconds and draws the monsters, you reappear 5–8 blocks away with 4 hearts, briefly invisible and resistant (every 10 minutes, every 6 at level 100; the raven must be within 32 blocks).

jtechstorage.guide.companion_look.title: Look and equipment
jtechstorage.guide.companion_look.body:
In the companion menu (K key), the Look tab customizes your companion – a large portrait shows every change right away. Everything is unlocked by its progress; the tooltip of each row names the requirements.

Coloring: Amethyst, Frost (level 20), Ember (200 defeated monsters), Jade (level 50), Gold (stage 3 and level 100), Soulbond (bond "Soulmate").

Body parts: the mantis' horns, the raven's tail, the shroom's cap – second form from level 30, third from level 60. At stage 3 also the wings, the crest or the back (backpack, cape or nothing).

Glow color: any color from the color bar (from level 10), plus default, white and pink.

Equipment: collar (+10% health per material), amulet (mantis +5% damage, shroom +10% healing, raven +1 block collection radius per material) and armor (+2 armor per material, plus toughness from netherite). Materials: iron (level 10), gold (25), diamond (45, stage 2), netherite (70), amethyst obsidian (100, stage 3). The bonus always comes from the best unlocked material – you can show any unlocked one, "Automatic" or nothing.
jtechstorage.guide.companion_bond.title: Bond
jtechstorage.guide.companion_bond.body:
The more time you spend with your companion, the closer your bond – and it never decreases. Stages: Stranger, Familiar (100), Friend (300), Partner (600), Soulmate (1000).

Feed: right-click with food of its kind (mantis: raw meat and fish; shroom: berries, mushrooms, bone meal; raven: seeds, gold nuggets). Its favorite food of the day is shown in the menu and gives +25 (once a day), other food +3 (five times a day).

Pet: button in the menu, +5, once per minute, ten times a day.

Play: throw a stick or an amethyst shard near it (Q) – it fetches it and brings it back: +10, ten times a day.

Rewards: gestures – Happy Hop (Familiar), Nuzzle (Friend) and a gesture of its own (Partner: Blade Salute, Shroom Dance, Bow). It shows them when it is happy; in the Look tab a click plays them. Soulmate unlocks the Soulbond coloring, the pink glow color and a pink aura (can be switched off). The HUD shows the bond stage as ❤ next to the level.

jtechstorage.guide.farm_tools.title: Farm tools
jtechstorage.guide.farm_tools.body:
Three blocks for your farms (iron, gold, mob, crop farms …).

Amethyst Hopper: like a hopper (outputs down or sideways, 5 slots, locked by redstone) but 16 times as fast – 8 items every 4 ticks – and it sucks in items lying in a 3×3 area above it.

Crystal Pusher: pushes items from the container behind it into the container in front of it, in all six directions, upwards too. The output faces where you look when placing it. Right-click: filter with 9 slots (empty = everything). Redstone stops it.

Farm Monitor: place it with its back against your farm's output chest. It counts what arrives (items per hour, chart of the last hour, most common items), turns red and messages you when nothing arrives for 5, 10 or 30 minutes or the chest is full. Its safe zone (8–32 blocks) keeps companions from attacking your farm's mobs. Clicked with a Storage Key, it shows up in the terminal under Statistics → Farms.

Chunk Loader: keeps its own chunk loaded, even while you're offline. Fuel: 1 amethyst shard per hour (amethyst block = 4 hours), hoppers can fill it. Without fuel it switches off and messages you. By default each player may have 25 active chunk loaders (config). Right-click shows the remaining time and, on request, the chunk borders.

jtechstorage.guide.amethyst_chests.title: Amethyst chests
jtechstorage.guide.amethyst_chests.body:
Bigger chests whose slots hold several stacks. They belong to your storage network like any chest – the terminal, the Amethyst Sprite, hoppers and Crystal Pushers all use them.

Amethyst Chest: 54 slots, 2 stacks each (chest, amethyst shards, copper).
Crystal Chest: 81 slots, 4 stacks each (Amethyst Chest, amethyst blocks, iron).
Resonance Chest: 108 slots, 8 stacks each (Crystal Chest, gold, diamonds).

Right-click a placed chest with a better one to upgrade it in place: the contents stay and you get the old chest back. Taking items out gives you at most one normal stack at a time. Unstackable items stay single. Break the chest and its contents drop as normal stacks.
